# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Please report security problems privately, never in a public issue or discussion.

Use **Report a vulnerability** on the repository's Security tab (GitHub private vulnerability reporting). Include what you found, how to reproduce it, the version, and the impact you see. Do not include real credentials or other people's data.

You can expect an acknowledgement within a few days and a fix or a clear plan as soon as it is understood. Please give us reasonable time to release a fix before you disclose publicly; we will credit you unless you prefer otherwise.

## Supported versions

Only the latest release receives security fixes. Opskest updates itself from signed releases, so staying current is the supported way to stay safe.

## What counts

In scope: the Opskest server, web interface, update system, and the Docker image and deployment files in this repository. Out of scope: vulnerabilities in third-party services you monitor, findings that need an already-compromised administrator account, and denial of service by an administrator against their own installation.
